title: Geographic differences in unemployment definitions
gist: The FRED Blog maps US state unemployment under each of the six BLS definitions (U-1 to U-6), showing regional rankings shift materially by definition: U-6 concentrates high underemployment in the West, while only California, Connecticut, Oregon, Washington and DC rank in the worst bucket on both U-1 and U-6.

insights.claim: US state unemployment rankings change materially depending on which of the six BLS definitions (U-1 through U-6) is used, so regional labour-market comparisons should specify the measure.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Regional consumer or credit analysis keyed only to headline U-3 can misread slack; check U-1 and U-6 state maps too.

insights.claim: Long-term unemployment (U-1, unemployed 15+ weeks) is lower in the US Mountain region, about average in the South and higher elsewhere.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Mountain-state labour markets look structurally tighter, supporting regional consumer and housing exposure.

insights.claim: On job-loser unemployment (U-2), Minnesota, Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas look somewhat worse and the Atlantic coast somewhat better than on long-term unemployment.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Elevated involuntary job losses in the central states flag layoff-driven stress there.

insights.claim: On headline U-3 unemployment, South-Central states have high rates, the Northeast looks better than on U-1/U-2, and Michigan stands out as elevated.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Michigan's standout headline unemployment is consistent with auto-sector weakness; a regional watchpoint.

insights.claim: Adding marginally attached workers (U-5) notably changes the picture for Hawaii and Illinois.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Hidden slack in Hawaii and Illinois is understated by the headline rate.
insights.locator: U-5: U-4 plus marginally attached workers

insights.claim: Under U-6, which adds involuntary part-timers, high US underemployment concentrates in the West, producing the largest visual change versus headline unemployment.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Western states carry more involuntary part-time slack than headline data show — relevant for regional wage pressure and consumer spending.

insights.claim: Only California, Connecticut, Oregon, Washington and Washington DC are in the worst category on both U-1 long-term unemployment and U-6 underemployment.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: These jurisdictions show slack on every measure — a consistent negative signal for local consumer credit and municipal revenues.
insights.locator: Only 5 locations are in the highest/darkest category

insights.claim: The Dakotas, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, Vermont and Wyoming are in the lowest category on both U-1 and U-6, marking them as the tightest US labour markets on every measure.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Persistently tight labour markets point to local wage pressure and resilient regional consumers.
insights.locator: Only 7 locations are in lowest/lightest category
